analysis_packet.certificate: Online cache objectives are coupled through admission and retention: broad recency favors object and byte hits on repeated locality but admits scans that displace reusable state; stronger scan resistance protects established reuse but can delay phase-shift adaptation and increase regret after workload changes. Byte hit rate additionally makes size-sensitive retention consequential, while object hit rate can favor numerous small objects. These tensions must be resolved under one-access-at-a-time information, with validity obligations acting as hard boundaries rather than optimization objectives. The anchor is contextual evidence of an inherited compromise, not an edit substrate.
exact_actions: Represent the objective interactions as causal tradeoffs rather than independent targets.
Carry scan pollution, reuse preservation, size effects, and phase staleness as one shared causal frame.
Treat interface legality, current-state eviction legality, capacity safety, and online visibility as non-negotiable boundary conditions.
Leave the anchor observational and avoid importing repair history or edit authority.
obligations: Preserve the specified Policy constructor and access interface.
Use only standard-library and online-visible information.
Return only unique integer keys currently cached by the evaluator.
Never cause cached bytes to exceed capacity_bytes.
Avoid benchmark, trace, oracle, reference-implementation, and external-library dependence.
Emit one directly generable policy lineage without score-based claims.
witnesses: Repeated locality benefits retention of recently reused objects.
One-pass scans create recency pressure without future reuse.
Phase changes make previously protected state stale and require online adaptation.
Variable object sizes couple byte utilization to object-count behavior.
Eviction legality depends on the evaluator's current cached state, not policy assumptions.
